request: what happens to the centroids in k-means each iteration?

composition.story: What happens to k-means centroids each iteration? Start with two guesses and four fixed points on a line. Assign each point to its nearest centroid, then move each centroid to its assigned points’ mean. Repeat these two steps until the centroids stop changing.

aha.observation: Each centroid moves to the arithmetic mean of its assigned points; the sample points stay fixed.

parts.presentation: Place below the explanation and above the experiment. Highlight the current state; the rail carries all progress information.

Render sample points as circles and centroids as labeled crosshairs on a separate aligned lane. Show sample identities and centroid names, without coordinate labels. Show membership using matching letters and colors, never color alone. Render each phase immediately, without animation. Assumptions: one-dimensional k-means, two clusters, nearest-centroid assignment, arithmetic-mean updates, no ties, and no empty clusters.
Anchor the callout to the centroid lane within the named region. Callout text identifies the change; its reason supplies the bound status line. Keep both free of numerical values.

Place compact readouts below the picture. Coordinates use data units, measured from the same axis origin. Display exact integers without rounding. Readouts contain all visible coordinate numbers. Centroid coordinates match the active phase; recentered coordinates are the arithmetic means of that phase’s assigned sample coordinates.
